claim: For every nondecreasing locally finite infinite sequence (a_i) of positive integers with bounded numerical multiplicity, if every tail has gcd one and its finite subset sums meet every residue class modulo every positive integer, liminf_{X->infinity} (log 2)#{i:a_i<=X}/log X>1, sum_i ||alpha a_i||^2=infinity for every irrational real alpha, (S_m-a_{m+1})/a_{m+1}^beta tends to positive infinity for every fixed real beta with 0<beta<1, where S_m=sum_{i=1}^m a_i, and for every integer K>=1 there exist disjoint finite subsets P,Q of {K,K+1,...} with sum_{i in Q}a_i-sum_{i in P}a_i=1, then there exist integers L>=0 and m_0>=1 such that for every m>=m_0, S_m>=2L and every integer in [L,S_m-L] is a subset sum of a_1,...,a_m using each labelled index at most once.

quadruple.statement: For every nondecreasing locally finite infinite sequence (a_i) of positive integers with bounded numerical multiplicity, if every tail has gcd one and its finite subset sums meet every residue class modulo every positive integer, liminf_{X->infinity} (log 2)#{i:a_i<=X}/log X>1, sum_i ||alpha a_i||^2=infinity for every irrational real alpha, (S_m-a_{m+1})/a_{m+1}^beta tends to positive infinity for every fixed real beta with 0<beta<1, where S_m=sum_{i=1}^m a_i, and for every integer K>=1 there exist disjoint finite subsets P,Q of {K,K+1,...} with sum_{i in Q}a_i-sum_{i in P}a_i=1, then there exist integers L>=0 and m_0>=1 such that for every m>=m_0, S_m>=2L and every integer in [L,S_m-L] is a subset sum of a_1,...,a_m using each labelled index at most once.
quadruple.stage: Locally finite labelled positive-integer sequences, legal finite signed sums, positive subset sums, modular arithmetic and real asymptotic limits.

shape.objects: Infinite countable nondecreasing positive-integer sequences with uniformly bounded numerical multiplicity. Prospective counterexamples are determined by finite geometric blocks with sparse endpoint modifications, extended by appending blocks under a fixed arithmetic rule. The sequence, finite subsets, floors and real limits have standard classical and Lean/Mathlib definitions. No rigidity theorem, random ensemble or spread family is recorded.
shape.quantifiers: For every such sequence, assume the full stated arithmetic and growth profile, including every fixed beta in (0,1), and a finite occurrence-respecting signed unit representation in every tail; then there exist fixed L and m_0 giving central-prefix coverage for all m>=m_0. The leading quantifier is universal, so one fully checked infinite sequence failing the conclusion refutes the inference.
shape.target_quantity: A yes/no sufficiency decision, not an extremal number. A fixed unspecified L suffices for the conclusion. A negative decision requires an infinite counterexample, not an unbounded sequence of sampled prefixes.
shape.ambient_structure: Order and additive arithmetic coexist. Appending a sparse block and its modified endpoint is the proposed recursive extension operation. It must preserve a digit-weight lower bound and supply a legal signed unit relation with growing support. No measurable ensemble, dependence statistic, structured intersection family or category transport is recorded.
shape.symmetries: Permuting equal-value occurrence labels preserves all properties. Dilation or translation need not preserve legal units or the full profile. No structured pieces with proved transport or intersection closure are recorded.
shape.configuration: Eventual coverage of every integer in every central prefix interval with a fixed endpoint loss. Truncation destroys the infinite quantified configuration and is not a certificate. The candidate extension must preserve increasing distinct levels, two labels per level, legal disjoint-support unit gadgets, digit-weight support bounds, all-prefix surplus and infinite norm divergence.
shape.extremal_candidate: A nonextremal sparse block floor-perturbation template is recorded in the strategy study, not yet a proved counterexample or an optimizing family. No optimum or rigidity is asserted.
shape.finite_certificates: One complete signed-identity block is the smallest nonempty block seed in the proposed template; a start parameter can be chosen and checked analytically after proving extension inequalities. No finite prefix certifies either side of the full infinite inference. Finite subset sums are computable but no finite reduction or mathematical computation is admitted.
shape.monotonicity: For a fixed valid prefix, increasing L weakens central coverage. This does not provide a finite stopping threshold for the entire infinite conjunction. No distinguished smallest open value of L is recorded.
shape.uniformity_parameter: Every sequence with the stated profile, every tail, every positive modulus, every irrational multiplier and each fixed beta in (0,1). Thresholds may depend on beta; no uniformity as beta approaches one is requested.
shape.proof_shape: A complete self-contained analytical counterexample candidate is written in moves/001-sparse-signed-blocks.md. The extension laws precede the first admissible disjoint-block seed. They prove legal unit identities with support length 4t+1 in every tail, all-prefix surplus growth against every fixed beta in (0,1), full tail modular coverage, noninteger squared-norm divergence, strict labelled counting, and numerical subset-sum upper density at most 1/9. Independent result review is pending.
shape.neighbours: The same generic strong-profile inference without legal signed unit identities is known false by accepted node-000006. Its two-copy coefficient-three relation does not verify the new antecedent. Graham 1964 Lemma 4 gives long intervals from signed units in every tail, not fixed-loss central coverage; Lemma 1 uses a separate smoothing supply. The pure-power signed profile, C1 and the original root remain open. Finite prefixes of the old and proposed templates are computable, without execution authority. No property-reflecting model equivalence or simpler verbatim model is known.
shape.known_bounds: The accepted earlier two-copy paired perturbation has labelled exponent log(4)/log(3), support count at most floor(X/9), all-sublinear-power surplus and arithmetic non-obstruction, but no proof of its legal signed unit condition. The new strategy study compresses a candidate into sparse endpoint modifications of b_j=3^j+floor(3^j/j), with disjoint long blocks and two copies. Graham's natural signed-tail amplification stops at long intervals, leaving central coverage unproved without a separate supply. No finite residue, first moment, shared-method metatheorem, recovered uniform constant, input-target equivalence or explicit threshold is recorded. Reserved move1 now provides a complete candidate with labelled exponent log(4)/log(3), legal all-tail signed integer coverage and arbitrarily long positive intervals, while #FS intersect [1,X]<=floor(X/9). All mathematical claims are analytical candidates pending independent result acceptance.
shape.missing_input: No mathematical input remains unproved in the written counterexample candidate; independent result review and immutable acceptance are pending. This decides only the exact auxiliary signed-tail inference and not the original pure-power objective.
shape.base_theory: ZFC and ordinary countable classical number theory. The prospective recursive construction and any elementary checks remain inside classical mathematics with choice, covered by Lean's standard foundations. There is no uncountable threshold, guessing principle, independence claim or extra axiom. No external standing hypothesis is imported.
